note: Two different legal entities were supplied under one name, so evidence is split. (1) B P IMPEX (Noida, UP) — real export shipments confirmed with dates, destinations, HS and B/L numbers, but the goods are garments (HS 62044290, 62045290, 39269069) and one auto part (fuel filler door, HS 73201011) — NOT the declared HS 870899. Per project rule 3 this is not a rejection ground: company stays in the base, actual HS codes are recorded, verdict would be accepted_hs_corrected. (2) OTTOTEK AUTOMOTIVE INDIA LLP (1/2 Shivaji Nagar, Gurugram) — ImportKey page 'Total Shipments 2881 Records detected', 'Latest Cargo 2026-02-13', but every visible row shows Ottotek as the BUYER/importer, e.g. '2026-02-13 | MAHLE AFTERMARKET GMBH | OTTOTEK AUTOMOTIVE INDIA LLP | OILCOOLER (COO-GERMANY) | Gdynia, GERMANY | NHAVA SHEVA SEA INNSA1, India | 87089900 | 7512710'. Its top port lanes (PALI ICD REWARI 151, Dammam 117, NHAVA SHEVA SEA 38, Gdynia 36, TUGLAKABAD ICD 18) are inbound lanes. No export row with Ottotek as shipper was seen, so for Ottotek specifically export_status is declared_only at best / none_found on the evidence read — no export bill of lading naming it as shipper was found. HS 870899 does match Ottotek's imported oil-cooler line, which suggests the declared HS belongs to the Ottotek side of the pair, not to B P Impex. Domestic supply evidence for both entities: not found in the sources read.
